sections.h2: What is Sandoval County, NM, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Sandoval County is the fourth-most populous county in New Mexico and part of the Albuquerque metropolitan area. Wikipedia reports 148,834 residents in the 2020 census, names Bernalillo as the county seat, and lists Rio Rancho as the other principal community.

The county was created in 1903 from the northern part of Bernalillo County, and its name comes from one of the large land-holding Spanish families in the area. It covers 3,716 square miles, and the highest point is the summit of Redondo Peak at 11,254 feet.

That geography produces two very different kinds of property: suburban lots in and around Rio Rancho, and larger rural or mountain parcels elsewhere in the county. Where a property sits determines which agencies appear on its tax bill.

sections.h2: What does Intel mean for Sandoval County?
sections.html:
Intel's Rio Rancho campus is the best-documented employer in the county. A 2021 press release from the governor's office said Intel planned a $3.5 billion investment and more than 700 new jobs at the site, and that the company had invested more than $16 billion in New Mexico since 1980.

The release quotes the county commission chair as saying the partnership began with a $2 billion industrial revenue bond in 1980 and has produced over 8,000 jobs, almost 5,000 of which went to New Mexico residents. It also says Intel spurred Rio Rancho's growth spurt in the 1980s.

These figures are from the 2021 announcement and are not current employment counts. For a house seller, the useful point is that a single large employer has shaped the Rio Rancho market for decades, and a Rio Rancho owner's sale timing can follow the local job market.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Sandoval County?
sections.html:
The Treasurer bills and collects, and the Assessor values. The county's Treasurer page gives the office at 1500 Idalia Road, Building D, Bernalillo, NM 87004, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

ItemDetail from the Treasurer's office
Phone505-867-7581 or toll free 1-800-332-8022
Emailtreasurers@sandovalcountynm.gov
MailP.O. Box 40, Bernalillo, NM 87004
Closed for staff meeting2:30 to 3:30 p.m., third Wednesday of each month

The office also gives a statement of taxes due on request, and payments by debit or credit card carry a convenience fee. The Treasurer asks for 72 hours for a payment to post.

sections.h2: Where does a Sandoval County tax dollar go?
sections.html:
Education takes the largest share. The Treasurer's chart for tax year 2025 shows 42 percent to education, 21 percent to municipal government, 20 percent to county government, 13 percent to the state, conservancy and other, and 5 percent to contracting hospitals.

The same page says the 2025 tax roll was $202.6 million, part of more than $1.483 billion the Treasurer is charged with collecting over ten years at a 99.22 percent collection rate. County programs funded include fire and 911, libraries, public safety, senior programs, roads, the landfill and the detention center. Where you live decides which agencies show up on your bill.

  • Education: 42 percent
  • Municipal government: 21 percent
  • County government: 20 percent
  • State, conservancy and other: 13 percent
  • Contracting hospitals: 5 percent

sections.h2: What is the Sandoval County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The county runs on a tax calendar rather than a regular one. The Treasurer's FAQ lists the dates that matter, and the Assessor's FAQ cites the statutes behind them.

DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; ownership and values are set as of this day
February 28Last day to report value changes, apply for exemptions or remove destroyed property
April 1Assessor mails the Notice of Value
October 1Tax roll goes from the Assessor to the Treasurer
November 1Tax bills mailed; the only bill the owner receives
November 10 to December 10First half due, without penalty through December 10
April 10 to May 10Second half due, without penalty through May 10
June 10Delinquent notices prepared and mailed
July 1Delinquency list for parcels over two years behind goes to the state

Late charges are 1 percent of the base tax per month in interest, plus 1 percent per month in penalty, with a penalty maximum of 5 percent and a minimum of $5. A returned check adds $25 or 5 percent of the check, whichever is greater.

sections.h2: How do Sandoval County owners keep their tax records correct?
sections.html:
Owners keep the record correct by telling the Assessor about changes in writing. The Treasurer's FAQ says any change of address must be submitted in writing and signed by the property owner on record with the Assessor, because bills go to the address on the Assessor's roll and may not be forwarded if more than six months have passed since a move.

The FAQ lists other reasons a bill may not arrive: a change of address received after bills were printed, a data entry error, or mail lost among the more than 100,000 bills the office sends. It also lists why a bill may rise: a higher assessed value, a lost exemption, a different school district, a higher mil levy or a voter-approved bond.

For a seller, a clean record speeds up a closing. Before listing or accepting an offer, confirm the owner of record, the mailing address and the status of both halves of the current year, then ask the Treasurer for a statement of taxes due.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Sandoval County valuation?
sections.html:
The protest window runs thirty days from the date the Notice of Value is mailed. The Assessor's FAQ describes the last day of that thirty-day period as the final date to file a valuation protest, to claim a family or veteran exemption, to apply for agricultural valuation, to report improvements costing more than $10,000 or to submit a statement of decrease in value.

The state's protest pamphlet sets the content of a petition: owner name and address, a property description, the reason the value is wrong and the value the owner believes is correct. A three-member county valuation protests board hears it and must decide within 180 days, and a decision can go to district court within thirty days.

The cap on residential increases also applies here: the higher of 103 percent of last year's value or 106.1 percent of the value two years back. A first-year valuation, new improvements and a change of ownership in the prior year are exceptions.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Sandoval County house is sold?
sections.html:
The county does not prorate property tax, and the bill follows the owner on record. The Treasurer's FAQ says taxes cannot be prorated and that a bill goes to every owner even when a mortgage company pays it. Because the division of the year between seller and buyer is not something the county does, it is settled in the sale paperwork instead.

Several practical points follow from that FAQ:

  • If the property is sold after October 1, the bill still carries the previous owner's name and address.
  • New owners should give the Assessor a mailing address as soon as the deed is recorded with the County Clerk.
  • A mobile home needs a tax release before a title transfer, paid in certified funds, and releases are by appointment only.
  • Property tax liability exists even if a bill was never received, under Section 7-38-36 NMSA 1978.

The Treasurer adds that the State of New Mexico and its counties do not run tax deed, tax certificate or tax lien sales. The only sales are state auctions for parcels with two or more years of delinquent tax. Cash Home Buyers works with Sandoval County owners who want to sell before that point, with no repairs and no commission.

faqs.q: Where is the Sandoval County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 1500 Idalia Road, Building D, in Bernalillo, NM 87004, on the first floor. Call 505-867-7581 or 1-800-332-8022, or write to P.O. Box 40, Bernalillo, NM 87004.

faqs.q: When are Sandoval County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and is paid without penalty through December 10. The second half is due April 10 and is paid without penalty through May 10.

faqs.q: What are the late fees on Sandoval County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is 1 percent of the base tax per month. The penalty is also 1 percent per month, capped at 5 percent, with a $5 minimum.

faqs.q: Will I get a bill if my mortgage company pays my tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Every property owner in Sandoval County is mailed a bill, even when the mortgage company pays it.

faqs.q: Does the county prorate property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer states taxes cannot be prorated. Sellers and buyers settle the split in their sale paperwork.

faqs.q: Can Sandoval County sell my house for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Not the county itself. The state conducts auctions for parcels with two or more years of delinquent property tax, and the Treasurer sends the delinquency list to the state on July 1.
